BG-1._basis_note: MEASURED, at fp32, 5x the worst drift this runtime shows against the fp32 reference over the frozen prompt set (rel L2 5.004e-4, max abs 6.539e-2). fp32 because that is where the end-to-end comparison has signal: in bf16 the reference reproduces ITSELF only to 0.37 relative L2, so the comparison measures the trajectory rather than the runtime. The dtype path is gated stage by stage instead, where a single stage has not had twenty steps to amplify anything. The 5x margin is a stated judgement, not a derivation.
BG-1._determinism_is_not_a_tolerance: The same build must reproduce ITSELF exactly or it cannot be a reference for anything. Only the comparison against the oracle has a tolerance.
BG-1.determinism_rule: byte-identical latents across replays of the same build

bf16_vs_bf16_oracle._what: This runtime against the reference, both bf16, end to end. Comparable to the reference's own 0.371 across dtypes -- which is why it is recorded and does not gate.

fp32_vs_fp32_oracle._what: This runtime in fp32 against the fp32 reference latents, same pinned noise. It is the evidence that the PIPELINE IS CORRECT: four stages that each agree to 1e-5 assemble into a generation that reproduces the reference to 5e-4.

reference_fp32_vs_reference_bf16._what: The reference against itself at two dtypes. No implementation difference at all. This is the cost of bf16 over twenty classifier-free-guided steps at 1024px, and it is the floor under any cross-dtype tolerance.

step_divergence_bf16._what: End-to-end bf16 divergence against the bf16 oracle by step count. It DECREASES with steps, which is the signature of the sampler's precision cliff at high sigma rather than of a defect: at the first step sigma is 157, so the x0 prediction is ~300 where the latent is ~1, and bf16 spacing there is ~2. issues/sampler-precision.md.

stage_tolerances_at_scored_dtype._margin: About 4x each measurement. The DiT's is looser because its disagreement grows with depth -- 0.005 at one block, 0.009 at four, 0.137 at twenty-eight -- so the threshold has to admit the full stack.
stage_tolerances_at_scored_dtype._what: Per-stage against the reference at the dtype the cells are scored in. These are the checks that cover the reduced-precision path, and they are sharp where the end-to-end comparison is not.

BG-2._basis_note: MEASURED. 5x the worst same-dtype drift between this runtime and the reference implementation at fp32, over the frozen prompt set. The multiple is a stated judgement: the measurement is a handful of prompts on one box and the quantity is amplified by a chaotic trajectory, so a threshold at the observed worst case would reject a correct implementation on the next prompt. Both the measurement and the multiple are recorded so the multiple can be disputed without re-running anything.
BG-2._looseness: Five times a drift that the 512px trajectory has already amplified. The relative L2 bound catches gross defects (past ones measured 1.20 and 1.37) and admits subtler ones, and the max-abs bound sits above the latents' own magnitude. A tighter gate for this generation would compare at fewer steps.
BG-2.determinism_rule: byte-identical latents across replays of the same build

fp32_step_divergence._what: This runtime in fp32 against fp32 reference latents made at the same step count, same pinned noise. It grows smoothly with steps, and the same prompts are worst at 4 and 20 steps: the denoise trajectory amplifies reduction-order rounding at 512px. A defect would already show at one step.

fp32_vs_fp32_oracle._what: This runtime against the reference at the SAME dtype. The only comparison that isolates implementation error from the cost of the dtype.

device._clocks_note: Clocks are not pinned and cannot be in a container. Only paired interleaved same-box deltas mean anything; absolute times from two different sessions are not comparable.
device.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090

stage_tolerances_at_scored_dtype._margin: About 4x each measurement. The DiT's is looser because its disagreement grows with depth -- 0.005 at one block, 0.009 at four, 0.137 at twenty-eight -- so the threshold has to admit the full stack.
stage_tolerances_at_scored_dtype._what: Per-stage against the reference at the dtype the cells are scored in. These are the checks that cover the reduced-precision path, and they are sharp where the end-to-end comparison is not.

_the_rule_that_was_learned_here: The gate must compare at the dtype the cell is SCORED in. BG-1 first compared a bf16 pipeline against an fp32 oracle and asked for 2% relative L2. That is unsatisfiable, and not by a little: the reference implementation compared against ITSELF at the two dtypes -- same weights, same pinned noise, same token ids, zero implementation difference -- comes out at 0.371 relative L2 (eval/cells/BG-1/dtype-cost.json). Comparing across dtypes measures the dtype, not the implementation.
_what_this_is: The correctness gate's thresholds, and where they came from. Kept in configs/ rather than hardcoded in the generation builder for the same reason the device peaks are: they should be set from a MEASUREMENT and regenerated, not typed and defended.
